statement: When a detector credits the FIRST file that matches in a sorted walk, a cited file also proves that every file sorting before it failed the predicate. Narrowing that predicate cannot rescue those earlier files, so a removed credit can only be replaced by a file sorting AFTER the citation. The baseline never read those files for that credit, so new reads (and new read-skip attributions) also happen only there. In the #433 preregistration this turned the cejel row's B6 prediction into a bounded case table instead of a guess: the human gate cited a Cejel certificate under leaderboard/reports/, and the fail-closed check cited a test file. Rule: when predicting a corpus delta for a narrowed predicate, read the citation and the walk order together, and state predictions as conditional on the after-citation range, which a report cannot show.

A disclosure field that reuses a signal's file-selection predicate changes whenever that predicate changes, even under a rubric where the mechanism that acts on it is switched off. In #433, A3's errorBoundaryFileReads gained isImplementationEvidencePath. That predicate also feeds withheldPaths[].signalsAdmitting, which v17 reports but never acts on, so a v17 report can lose 'A3.prod_readiness_primitives' from a withheld calibration-path entry. Neither #441's changelog entry nor a scoring-level comparison would surface this. Rule: for a byte-level prediction, grep every call site of a changed predicate, including disclosure-only call sites gated off for the rubric under test, and list each field it can move.

A goal card's description of a precedent's protocol is a summary, not the record. The #433 card said the 0.4.9 and 0.4.11 runs used 'depth-1, blob-filtered' checkouts. The recorded prepare-checkouts.sh fetches --depth=1 with no --filter, and the 0.4.11 harness file it said to copy named the private row in code, which the same card forbids. Rule: before reusing a precedent, read its recorded commands and files, and follow the record. Write each disagreement with the card into the preregistration, and re-read copied files against the current card's disclosure rules before committing them.
